thought_title: Self-knowledge, humility, and life in Christ
orientation: These closing sayings continue the alphabetical maxims on purifying the soul from passions and attaining union with Christ by keeping his commandments.
pass_a_gloss: When you wish to know yourself who you are, do not compare who you were, but what you have become from the beginning. A vainglory soul is a waterless pit. A pride soul is an inn of robbers, and it hates the sound of knowledge. Of a true man, bad wandering is the not to know the Scriptures. If you fear God, know it from your tears. Humility of soul is an unbreakable weapon. A man loving virtue is a tree of paradise. Jesus Christ is a tree of life; use him as one must and you will certainly not die into the age. Do good to those who are truly poor and you will eat Christ. To eat the body of Christ is true strength. If you love Christ, you will not forget to keep his commandments; for from there a benefactor is made to appear after God. The friend according to God flows milk and honey by his true words, but a lazy soul will not have such a friend. A reasoning loving pleasure is a cruel master. To be silent about the truth is to bury gold. The one fearing God does all things according to God.

choices.why: Brief glossary fixes φιλόδοξος to vainglory, kept literally without polishing to vainglorious.
Brief glossary fixes ὑπερήφανος to pride, kept as literal predicate noun.
Brief glossary requires Scriptures for Γραφαί.
Brief glossary requires commandments for ἐντολαί.
ξύλον is tree or wood; tree fits paradise context and cast description.

pass_b_english: When you want to know who you are, do not measure yourself against who you were. Consider what you have become from the beginning. A soul full of vainglory is a dry cistern. A soul full of pride is an inn for robbers, and it hates the sound of knowledge. For a true man, not to know the Scriptures is a grievous error. If you fear God, you will know it by your tears.

The humility of the soul is an unbreakable weapon. A man who loves virtue is a tree of paradise. Jesus Christ is the tree of life. Use him as you ought, and you will never die. Help those who are truly poor, and you will eat Christ. True strength is to eat the body of Christ.

If you love Christ, you will not forget to keep his commandments. For it is from there that a benefactor after God appears. A friend according to God flows with milk and honey with true words, but a lazy soul will have no such friend. A thought that loves pleasure is a cruel master. To keep silent about the truth is to bury gold. Whoever fears God does everything according to God.
notes: Source has minor OCR defects: missing space after numbers, missing accents in ανυδρος for ἄνυδρος and οντως for ὄντως, ∆ for Δ, and stray page numbers 1 and 2; gloss follows the readable text without inventing missing words.

problems.why: Transitive σιγᾶν means to keep silent about or leave unspoken, not to silence or suppress something.
problems.fix: To keep silent about the truth
problems.ruling: Σιγᾶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν is to keep silent about truth; 'silence the truth' wrongly suggests active suppression.

edits.old: To silence the truth is to bury gold.
edits.new: To keep silent about the truth is to bury gold.

fixed: Fixed mistranslation of Σιγᾶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν: changed active suppression to keeping silent about.
